subject: ss-medical-oncology
title: Infusion reactions, hypersensitivity and extravasation: mechanisms, premedication and specific antidotes

steps.tx: Formulation excipients in cytotoxic taxane preparations trigger acute pseudo-allergic infusion events. Taxane paclitaxel **hypersensitivity reactions** are classic Type I IgE-independent anaphylactoid reactions driven by massive complement activation from the lipid vehicle solvent **Cremophor EL**. Mandatory standard premedication comprising intravenous **dexamethasone**, H1-antihistamines diphenhydramine, and H2-blockers ranitidine administered 30 to 60 minutes prior to paclitaxel infusion reduces severe anaphylactoid reaction rates from 30% to under 2%.
steps.say: Formulation excipients in cytotoxic taxane preparations trigger acute pseudo-allergic infusion events. Taxane paclitaxel hypersensitivity reactions are classic Type I IgE-independent anaphylactoid reactions driven by massive complement activation from the solvent Cremophor EL. Mandatory premedication with dexamethasone, diphenhydramine, and H2-blockers administered prior to infusion reduces severe anaphylactoid reactions to under 2%.

left.title: Paclitaxel (Cremophor EL)
points: Peak onset during first or second cycle (first 10 min)
Slow initial infusion rate (titrated over 3 hours)

right.title: Nab-Paclitaxel (Abraxane)
points: Completely devoid of Cremophor EL or polyoxyethylated castor oil
Zero steroid or antihistamine premedication required

steps.tx: Repeated exposure to heavy metal coordination complexes promotes classical immunological sensitization. Platinum carboplatin and oxaliplatin hypersensitivity reactions represent true **Type I IgE-mediated** allergic responses that typically emerge after 6 or more treatment cycles following cumulative antigen sensitization. For patients with high-risk clinical needs who cannot substitute the platin backbone, successful re-treatment is accomplished via standardized multi-bag intravenous **desensitization** protocols in an intensive care setting.

nodes.label: Specific IgE Formation against Platinum Adducts

steps.tx: Accidental subcutaneous infiltration of intravenous cytotoxics carries severe prognostic consequences based on drug class. Cytotoxic **extravasation injuries** are categorized as **vesicants**, which cause cellular death, blister formation, and progressive severe tissue necrosis; irritants, which provoke burning discomfort and superficial phlebitis without deep necrosis; and non-vesicants, which cause neither ulceration nor tissue necrosis. Extravasation of DNA-binding vesicants like anthracyclines leads to unremitting, deepening ulceration.

Cytotoxic extravasation injuries are categorized as vesicants, which cause cellular death and severe tissue necrosis; irritants, which provoke burning without necrosis; and non-vesicants, which produce no ulceration. Extravasation of DNA-binding vesicants leads to unremitting, deepening ulceration.

rows: Cell death, retained in tissues, deepening necrosis
Severe venous inflammation, necrosis if high volume

steps.tx: Anthracycline tissue infiltration represents the most destructive chemotherapy extravasation emergency. Inadvertent **Anthracycline** doxorubicin extravasation mandates immediate cold pack application to induce localized vasoconstriction, followed by intravenous infusion of the specific antidote **dexrazoxane**. Administered over 3 consecutive days within 6 hours of extravasation, dexrazoxane enters affected tissues, binds topoisomerase II, chelates iron, and prevents free radical-induced soft tissue sloughing, reducing surgical debridement rates by over 95%.

steps.tx: Extravasation of plant alkaloid mitotic inhibitors requires diametrically opposite physical thermal management. Inadvertent **Vinca alkaloid** vincristine or vinblastine extravasation requires dry warm compress application to promote local vasodilation and drug dispersal away from the injection site. This is immediately accompanied by localized subcutaneous infiltration of **hyaluronidase**, which enzymatically breaks down intercellular hyaluronic acid in the extracellular matrix, facilitating rapid tissue reabsorption and systemic clearance.

left.title: Anthracycline Extravasation
points: Localizes drug and minimizes cellular uptake

right.title: Vinca Alkaloid Extravasation
points: Avoid cold packs (causes drug retention and ulceration)

steps.tx: Alkylating nitrogen mustard extravasation produces rapid dermal blistering and microvascular thrombosis. Extravasation of **Mechlorethamine** mustine is neutralized by emergency local subcutaneous injection of 1/6th molar **sodium thiosulfate**. Thiosulfate provides an excess of highly reactive nucleophilic substrate, rapidly reacting with the highly unstable aziridinium ion alkylating intermediates to chemically inactivate the vesicant before irreversible cross-linking of dermal and endothelial cellular macromolecules can take place.

nodes.label: Prevention of Dermal Sloughing and Ulceration

steps.tx: Central venous access devices protect peripheral arm veins from caustic vesicant damage. **Totally implantable venous access ports** TIVAP significantly decrease peripheral extravasation hazards, but require strict aseptic Huber needle cannulation, routine post-infusion **heparin flushing**, and regular verification of brisk blood return before beginning any cytotoxic infusion. If resistance to aspiration occurs, contrast portography is mandatory to exclude catheter tip fracture, fibrin sheath formation, or port-catheter disconnect.

Resistance to aspiration requires contrast portography to exclude catheter problems.

rows: Can infuse fluids freely but unable to aspirate blood
Intermittent postural infusion resistance at clavicle
Neck or chest wall swelling during infusion
Arm edema, dilated collateral chest wall veins

steps.tx: Monoclonal antibody administration is complicated by target-mediated systemic immune activation. **Infusion-related reactions** during initial rituximab, obinutuzumab, or daratumumab infusions are driven by acute **cytokine release** of TNF-alpha, IL-6, and interferon-gamma from opsonized circulating lymphocytes. Clinical management requires temporary infusion interruption, slow re-escalation, and intravenous diphenhydramine, intravenous hydrocortisone, and oral paracetamol premedication, with severe bronchospasm or refractory hypotension treated as life-threatening anaphylaxis with intramuscular adrenaline.

Management requires temporary infusion interruption, slow re-escalation, and premedication with diphenhydramine, hydrocortisone, and paracetamol.

nodes.label: Resume at 50% Speed Once Symptoms Resolve

steps.tx: Reactions are classified by timing and severity, and the **immunopathology** is mainly **type I IgE-mediated**, with platinum-specific IgE found in a large share of moderate to severe cases. Skin testing has a poor negative predictive value, so diagnosis remains largely clinical. Serum tryptase is useful only as supportive evidence during an acute event.
